lower_bound.quote:
Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains
no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on \(v\) vertices already uses at
least \(v\) edges; hence every connected component \(C\) has \(e_C=v_C-1\) and
is a tree (an isolated vertex counts as a tree). We use the component
containing the vertex of \(a_q\).
lower_bound.witness: Counterexample: take q=2, a_1=1/5 and a_2=4/5. Xiang uses one cut, splitting a_2 into 2/5 and 2/5. Then x=(2/5,2/5,1/5), so the sole rank-pair edge is a loop at vertex a_2. Thus the graph has one edge on two vertices, yet contains a loop; moreover the selected component containing a_q=a_2 has v=1 and e=1 and is not a tree, so the asserted bipartition is unavailable.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The proof of D≥Γ for every Xiang refinement depends on bipartitioning the selected component. Section 4 explicitly invokes this lower half of the refinement lemma to obtain Liu's all-n guarantee.

parsed.notes: The closed form is correct. The drafting reduction and Xiang construction are valid, but the claimed graph acyclicity is false, leaving the matching lower bound unproved as written.
